title: Giovanni Battista Spinelli, Count of Cariati, to Pedro de Urrea, Venice, 16 April 1512, two letters (catalogue 2865): news after Ravenna in a letter cipher with glosses of the time, read in part with a key rebuilt from one letter's glosses and tested on the other's

system.summary: A homophonic letter substitution of about 40 signs (letter- and figure-like shapes, barred variants, dot signs) set inside clear Italian; 7 and a barred p bracket the runs; one code sign (Nplus) for '(lo) papa'.
system.notes: Nulls: 7, ptop and dot. The single code sign is read from the glosses only (no tested value).

prior_solution.where: Glosses of the time on both leaves (over most cipher lines, not letter for letter). No modern reading found (catalogue 2865 says no decipherment; web search 28 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling set the task and the rules (plan stamped before key work, two blind readers, a held-out test stamped by FreeTSA before it was run). AI agents fetched the images, transcribed, built the key, ran the test, read and wrote. No person has checked the transcription, the key or the reading against the images.

solution.what: Both DARA PDFs fetched by curl (04:11 UTC); page images extracted.
Two blind transcriptions by helper agents with their own sign names; 700 of 727 signs agree.
The two letters compared for shared cipher runs: none longer than six signs (scripts/shared_runs.py), so no crib from repetition.

Key built by hand from letter B only, aligning its glosses (venendo lo S. Prospero, lo real tutto venuto in mano de villani, sei milia, sono morti asai deli nostri principali, se acordaria con re de francia ...). Plan amended first (roles of the letters swapped) because this started on the letter planned as held out.

Held-out test under the proposed rule #1014 on letter A's glossed lines: frozen in verification/MANIFEST_v1.sha256 (SHA-256 9ac2da72eba4a20f8c26ba25df68ab28cab527569aa1ff353d62841b27acbbdf), stamped by FreeTSA 04:47:00 UTC, measured once 04:47:04: 0.725 of gloss letters against a best of 0.323 for 200 shuffled keys (z 15.5). PASS.

Both letters decoded and read word by word (reading_words.tsv): first count A 64 of 82, B 71 of 81 cipher words sure; recounted in the cold check below. Values proposed after the test (hbar = s, fbar = r, Nplus = papa, o = b in A) are not covered by it.

Cold check after the test, by a separate AI agent (Claude Opus 5.5) from about 05:00 UTC: one fresh helper agent, shown only the page images and the 25 places where the two readers differ (no key, no reading), ruled on each (05:05-05:18 UTC; 8 for the first reader, 10 for the second, 1 neither, 6 not told). The word count was then redone against the decode: A 62 of 83, B 70 of 81 cipher words sure. A third [papa] code (A2.10) was counted; e (A1.02), spagnioli (A2.08) and de (B1.02) rest on a disputed sign and are probable; lle and llo are written as the key gives them.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the glosses of the time on letter B and tested on letter A against letter A's glosses (held-out test passed). Every word counted as read is given by the key; in letter A (held out) the key was built without it, and the glosses there agree with most of it; in letter B the key was fitted to the glosses, so the glossed words of B are read from the gloss as well as the key. Where gloss and decode differ, the decode is given. No word is counted as read from a gloss alone.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_words.tsv: cipher words only, 132 of 164 sure (A 62/83, B 70/81); one model reader, recounted by a cold-check AI agent on 28 Nov 2026 (a third [papa] counted, disputed signs made probable).

texts.label: Letter A, Venice, 16 Apr 1512
texts.summary: After Ravenna: the Council of Ten met with the Giunta; Spinelli encouraged the Signoria to hearten the Pope; to treat with the Pope they would want the ten thousand Spanish foot made up with Italians and forty thousand ducats.

texts.label: Letter B, Venice, 16 Apr 1512
texts.summary: The Viceroy to go to Naples and bring the army back to the field; Prospero Colonna with three hundred men at arms; the royal train fell to peasants; many principal men dead; if the French took Milan and did not restore it to the Emperor, they would come to terms with France.
